chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife with one divorce while she was pure, then kept her in his house until she had two menstruations and became pure, then divorced her with two divorces while she was pure. He said: This is if she had three menstruations from the day he divorced her with the first divorce, then she has become lawful for marriage.

But how should I act or say this? And in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is narrated that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, give me a ruling regarding myself. He said: Regarding what shall I give you a ruling? She said: My husband divorced me while I was pure, then kept me so he did not have sexual intercourse with me, until I menstruated and became pure, then he divorced me with another divorce. Then he kept me so he did not have sexual intercourse with me, except that he uses me (for intimacy) and sees my hair, my neck, and my body, until I menstruated the third time and became pure, then he divorced me with the third divorce.

He said, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: O woman, do not marry until you have had three fresh menstruations. For the three menstruations you had while you were in his house, you only had them while you were in his bonds (of marriage).

What the main part of this narration contains is that if he divorces her with one divorce at each menstruation, then she observes the waiting period from the first divorce. The meaning of this is that if he divorces her a second time without revocation (regaining her), then his divorce does not take effect (as a final divorce), and the waiting period is upon her from the first divorce.

And what he narrated at the end of the narration, which he found in the book of Ali (peace be upon him), admits two possibilities: One is that it was permissible because he revoked her (regained her) then divorced her, so the waiting period was upon her from the final divorce, if the divorces were according to the Sunnah as we have explained.

And the other possibility is that it is based on precaution (Taqiyyah), because among the jurists there are those who permit the three divorces one after another at each menstruation even if he did not revoke her at all, so this would be consistent with those who followed this opinion.

And that which indicates the distinction, which we preceded, is that in the Sunnah divorce this is permissible, but it is not permissible in the divorce of the waiting period except after sexual intercourse.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّة: Sunnah divorce (divorce during purity without intercourse)
key_terms.مُرَاجَعَة: Revocation (regaining the wife without new contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a second divorce if a man divorces his wife, keeps her, and divorces her again without sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *Talaq al-Sunnah* by distinguishing between revocable and final divorces, emphasizing that a second divorce without prior sexual intercourse (*Muwafaqah*) does not count as a distinct event but rather extends the waiting period of the first. It reconciles apparent contradictions in the *Book of Ali* by offering two scholarly interpretations: either the husband had already consummated the marriage, or the narration reflects *Taqiyyah* to align with schools that accept triple divorce in single sessions. Ultimately, it establishes that for a divorce to be considered final and effective after revocation, sexual intercourse is a mandatory condition.
